extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, publicists, startup founders, and anyone who pitches journalists/media
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for composing email/social pitches and press-release outreach that get journalists to open, respond, and write stories. Focuses on subject lines, first sentences, story angle, spokesperson credibility, multimedia, timing, and relationship-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line all CAPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line that's all CAPS
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists often delete pitches immediately if the subject is all caps; it's perceived as spammy or shouting.

rubrics_metrics.name: False URGENT/BREAKING claims
rubrics_metrics.description: "URGENT" or "BREAKING" when it's not
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking a non-urgent pitch as 'URGENT' or 'BREAKING' erodes trust and leads to immediate deletion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template greeting failure
rubrics_metrics.description: "Hi [FIRST NAME]" — template fail
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obvious mail-merge placeholders or generic greetings signal mass blasts and reduce credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line longer than preview
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line longer than the preview shows
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the important information is after the preview cutoff, the pitch may be skipped; keep key info early in the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unknown sender with no signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Sender name I don't recognize + no signature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a recognizable sender name and a clear signature (company, role, contact info) to establish legitimacy quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch about recently covered topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch about something I covered last week
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid re-pitching topics the journalist has recently covered unless you have a genuinely new angle or significant update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehashing an already-used angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Story angle I've already done
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your angle is effectively identical to one the reporter has already published, clarify what new element or evidence makes it worth revisiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unverifiable spokesperson credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Spokesperson with no credentials I can verify
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verifiable credentials (titles, links, prior media, LinkedIn) for spokespeople to establish authority; lack of verification reduces response likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic 'innovative product' framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic "innovative new product" framing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid bland marketing phrases; explain specifically why the product, service, or data matters and to whom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of a clear story angle
rubrics_metrics.description: No clear story angle, just announcement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches should present a clear, newsworthy angle (what's new, surprising, consequential) and not read like a bland announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific-number or named-entity subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject that mentions a specific number or named entity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects that include concrete facts (numbers, named customers, notable names) attract attention more than vague claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: First sentence shows reporter knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: First sentence references my recent work / shows knowledge of my work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a line that demonstrates you've read the reporter's past coverage (cite a recent story) to show relevance and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear story angle with verification path
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear story angle with verification path
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the angle succinctly and give obvious ways the reporter can verify claims (data sources, spokespeople, documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson availability within 24 hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Spokesperson available within 24 hours
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists value immediacy—note spokesperson availability and time zones; promise and deliver quick availability if you claim it.

rubrics_metrics.name: One specific, time-bound ask
rubrics_metrics.description: One specific ask, time-bound
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a single, clear request (e.g., interview at X time, embargoed data for tomorrow) rather than vague asks; include deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthy prior source relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Trustworthy source I've worked with before
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the source or PR has previously provided solid information, mentioning that track record increases the chance of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch anticipates editor's questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch that anticipates my editor's questions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address likely follow-up questions proactively (methodology, caveats, context) to make the reporter's job easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia pre-attached
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-attached multimedia (no asking for it)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach images, video, or charts up front when relevant so reporters don't have to request them; makes the pitch more usable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer/partner reference ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer/partner reference ready
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references or case studies that reporters can contact for verification or quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder/CEO personally available
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder/CEO personally available
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of senior leadership for comment can increase perceived newsworthiness—state direct availability if true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with publication voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Story that fits my publication's voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor the pitch to the outlet's angle, audience, and tone; a good fit increases the chance of assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'just following up' follow-ups
rubrics_metrics.description: "Just following up" emails (62% of journalists hate this)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-ups should add value (new info, new availability) rather than generic reminders; otherwise they annoy reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't CC large lists
rubrics_metrics.description: PR firms cc'ing 10 people on pitch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass cc'ing looks like bulk outreach and reduces personalization; send targeted emails instead of large group CCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo must include real exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargo with no exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering an embargo without any meaningful exclusivity or advance access frustrates journalists; be clear and honest about exclusivity terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Exclusive' should be exclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: "Exclusive" pitched to 50 journalists simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling something 'exclusive' while pitching many reporters defeats the term and damages trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid long spokesperson bios in pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Long bio paragraphs about the spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep bios concise; include a short relevant credential line and link to a fuller bio if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver promised follow-up materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to send follow-up materials promised
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you promise assets or data, deliver them promptly; failing to do so harms credibility and future coverage chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pitching during major news events
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitching during major news events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of news cycles—pitching during big breaking news means lower attention for your story unless it's directly relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build relationships not lists
rubrics_metrics.description: "Build relationships, not lists"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate long-term, individualized relationships with reporters rather than one-off mass outreach; relationship capital yields better outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect journalists' time
rubrics_metrics.description: "Respect my time and I'll respect yours"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise, accurate, and responsive; showing respect for reporters' time fosters mutual trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-sentence 'why care' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you can't tell me why I should care in 2 sentences, I won't"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey the news hook in one or two sentences up front; if the value isn't immediately obvious, the pitch will be discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty about offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: "Honesty about what you can and can't offer"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about availability, exclusivity, data limitations, or what spokespeople can provide; dishonesty ends relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Once you burn me, we're done
rubrics_metrics.description: "Once you burn me, we're done"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated misleads, missed materials, or false claims can permanently close off a reporter to future pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line should be specific and accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line specific and accurate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise, accurate subject that communicates the core news or hook rather than vague or hyperbolic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson must be credible and available
rubrics_metrics.description: Spokesperson available and credible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine verifiable credibility (title, past work, references) with prompt availability to increase likelihood of placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a verification path
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear story angle with verification path
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sources, data links, documents, or named references that allow a reporter to quickly verify claims.
